plan.title: hooks: one start-up guard order and one recovery message table for the host-hook outer, deft-hook and hook-bin

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan group G-G (story id ovpr-g-message-table): units P4-U3a + P4-U3b + P4-U3d in one PR. Primary issue #6620; also #6466, #5940, #6225, #5977 (item 2), #6517, #6550. Directive can be reached through the committed .mjs hook file, the global deft-hook, the runtime hook-bin, the directive launcher and launcher doctor, the git-hook helper, the Taskfile and the runtime bin. Each checks things in a different order and prints different advice (the global pair, '(or yarn)', plain `pnpm install` that the hook refuses, `@?`, `deft update`, a retired `_deft-run.sh`). Build one start-up guard order and one message table in core (with a byte-identical launcher copy), and use it at every entry point, with the exact RC-06 / RC-12 words in plain customer language.
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

When Directive can't run, an agent host reaches it three ways: the committed `.mjs` hook file, the global `deft-hook` command (old repos), or the runtime's `hook-bin.js`. Each one checks things in a different order and prints different advice. The same broken state gets different instructions, and some of them don't work.

In a fresh clone or a new linked worktree, `node_modules` is missing, so the hooks fail closed (AC9.12). Agent workflows create worktrees all the time, so this is frequent. The message must say plainly that a person runs the project install in a terminal, because the agent's own shell is blocked (#6466, D-013).

Evidence (origin/master `def527f5e`):
- **`.mjs` outer** (`hostHookOuterSource()`, `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts:259`): untracked disable flag → quiet allow; `hook-bin.js` missing → fail closed; spawn failure → fail closed. Text `HOST_HOOK_MISSING_PIN_PROJECT_PM_GUIDANCE` (`:22-24`): "Run npm install or pnpm install (or yarn) in this project." Yarn is not supported, and the text doesn't say that a person must run it.
- **Global `deft-hook`** (`packages/cli/src/hook-launcher.ts`, 64 lines): no disable-flag check, no old-layout check. Every failure prints `RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` (`:27`, `:36`, `:49`) = "npm i -g @deftai/directive, then directive install --repair" (`packages/cli/src/constants.ts:34`). The docstring at `:4` still says host configs should call `hook-bin.js` directly (superseded by AC9.1 v261027).
- **Runtime `hook-bin`** (`run()`, `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts:386`): root check, then the pin check (`:446`), then self-complete, then `decideHook`. The disable flag is checked only inside `decideHook` (Scott's `dispatcher.ts`), after the pin checks. Through global `deft-hook` or an old direct `hook-bin.js` registration, a disabled project with a pin mismatch is blocked instead of stopping quietly. The fallback text is `cheap.recoveryGuidance ?? INSTALLATION_RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` (`:462`).
- **Install commands:** the #6313 admit lets through only `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `npm install` and `npm ci` (`PIN_MISMATCH_RECOVERY_COMMANDS`, `packages/core/src/install-health/recovery-admit.ts`). `PIN_MISMATCH_PROJECT_PM_RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` (`packages/core/src/install-health/constants.ts:34`) names plain `pnpm install`, which the hook refuses.
- **Shipped since the unit spec was written (effef711d):**
  - #6534 (#6375) added `renderPinMismatchRecoveryGuidance` (`packages/core/src/install-health/pin-mismatch-guidance.ts:70`), used by `hook-dispatch.ts:458-461` when pin ≠ installed is the only fault. It names the project root, says to open a terminal outside the blocked session, and names `pnpm install` / `npm install` by lockfile kind.
  - #6563 (#6185) added `FOREIGN_RUNTIME_LINK_RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` (`constants.ts:51`).

## What the design says

- AC9.12 (v261027): the same guard order on the host-hook outer, the git-hook helper, the Taskfile entry and launcher commands that delegate to the pin: (1) untracked `.deft-directive-disable` → stop with no pin policy load; (2) missing or unusable pin package → fail closed with clear **project** `npm install` / `pnpm install` guidance; (3) run the pin.
- AC9.1 (v261027): the outer uses only Node built-ins until the guards pass; full product logic stays in `hook-bin.js`.
- AC2.6 / AC9.4 / AC14.8: pin ≠ installed → no setup, no policy, block.
- Ledger "Unified local entry guards": same order, same recovery shape, minimal duplication.
- §A9: a new launcher never delegates to an old-style runtime.
- D-001 (Rule 3): one shared guard and one message table; failures block on every host.
- D-013: no runtime → fail closed on every entry point. No install is let through on that path (the #6328 admit applies only when `hook-bin` runs). The message says a person runs the project install in a terminal. Borrowing another checkout's runtime is ruled out (AC9.5).
- D-017 (O-37): #6375's shipped Codex wording (#6534) is checked against the table here. P4-U4 is dropped.
- Open, settled before merge: the exact words from P4-U2 / RC-06 (O-30: which install commands the message names); O-34 / RC-07 (old-layout check before "runtime missing").

## Expected

1. **One message table in core** (`packages/core/src/install-health/constants.ts`): `EntrySituation`, `ENTRY_GUARD_MESSAGES` and `projectInstallCommand(projectRoot)` (reads lockfile presence only). Rows follow the Rule 3 table; final words come from P4-U2:
   - `disabled`: no message; allow / exit 0.
   - `runtime-missing`: names the missing runtime package and says a person runs `{install}` in this project, in a terminal, because the agent's shell is blocked. Blocks.
   - `pin-mismatch`: installed X is not the pinned Y; run `{install}`. Blocks; the named install is admitted (#6313).
   - `wiring-damaged`: `directive install --repair` (doctor and launcher only; hooks self-complete).
   - `data-behind`: reuse `SESSION_START_SCHEMA_BEHIND_NOTICE`. Notice only.
   - `legacy-layout`: "This repo uses pre-OVPR Directive. Run `directive upgrade`, or keep the old tools: `npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.126.2`." Blocks.
   - `launcher-missing`: `npm i -g @deftai/directive` (text for committed surfaces).
   - `hook-failed`: P1-U1's `HOST_HOOK_NONDECISION_REASON`, moved unchanged.
   - `contract-too-new`, `root-mismatch`, `overlay`, `pin-invalid`, `no-runtime-pin`: existing text, moved unchanged.

   `{install}` is `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `npm install` with `package-lock.json`, else "`npm install` (or `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`)", subject to O-30. Drop "(or yarn)". Keep the old constant names as aliases. Leave `INSTALLATION_RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` unchanged here; its callers move in P4-U3c / P4-U3d.
2. **One order**, in a doc comment above the table and in a shared test fixture: disabled → root-mismatch (hooks only) → legacy-layout (only when the root `package.json` has no `@deftai/directive-runtime` dependency; P1-U2's recogniser; subject to O-34 / RC-07) → runtime-missing → pin-mismatch (+ #6313 admit) / overlay → contract-too-new (launcher only) → wiring-damaged → data-behind.
3. **Use it in the three hook entry points:**
   - `.mjs` outer: embed the `runtime-missing` row with the lockfile-based `{install}`, using Node built-ins only. The outer keeps its two checks (disabled, runtime missing). Don't add a pin ≠ installed check to the outer. Use P1-U1's block helper unchanged.
   - Global `deft-hook`: Node check → discovery → **disabled** (new) → **legacy** (P1-U2) → runtime missing → `hook-bin` missing (as `runtime-missing`) → spawn the installed `hook-bin`. Replace every `RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` use with table rows. Block via P1-U2's `renderHookBlock`. Fix the stale docstring.
   - `hook-dispatch.ts` `run()`: after the `session.end` branch, if the disable flag is active (`isDeftDirectiveDisableActive`), skip the root, pin and self-complete steps and go straight to `decideHook`. Build the deny text from the table.
   - Check the shipped #6375 text (`renderPinMismatchRecoveryGuidance`) against the `pin-mismatch` row (D-017).
4. **Launcher copy:** `packages/cli/src/entry-guard.ts`, a byte-identical copy of the table and `projectInstallCommand`, with no imports beyond `node:fs` / `node:path` (AC3.1). A parity test keeps the copies equal. P4-U3b uses it.

Must not do: no product logic or #6313 admit in the `.mjs` outer (AC9.1); don't widen the admit list; no install admit on the missing-runtime path (D-013); don't edit `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` (Scott); don't redo P1-U1 (exit codes, block forms) or P1-U2 (recogniser) — move only their reason strings, and add a parity test for the two block renderers; don't run old-layout code; don't change the registered command form or sha8 naming (AC9.1); don't adopt #6358.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One table (`ENTRY_GUARD_MESSAGES`) in core and one copy in cli. The parity test fails on any drift.
2. The outer, `deft-hook` and `hook-dispatch` all check the untracked disable flag before any pin check. Tests cover each.
3. In an old-layout fixture, `deft-hook` prints the `legacy-layout` row and blocks per host. It never spawns anything.
4. With `node_modules` deleted, the outer and `deft-hook` print the `runtime-missing` row with the lockfile-correct command, say a person runs it in a terminal, and block per host.
5. With pin ≠ installed (runtime built from this change), `hook-bin` denies with the `pin-mismatch` row, and the exact command it names is admitted.
6. No string in the three hook entry points contains `npm i -g @deftai/directive, then` or "(or yarn)".
7. The `.mjs` outer still uses Node built-ins only before loading `hook-bin` (existing outer tests stay green).

Tests: new `packages/cli/src/entry-guard-parity.test.ts`; extend `packages/cli/src/hook-launcher.test.ts` (created by P1-U2); update `host-hook-outer.test.ts`, `hook-dispatch.test.ts`, `hook-identity-failclosed.test.ts`, `recovery-admit.test.ts` (every command the `pin-mismatch` row can name passes `matchPinMismatchRecoveryCommand`) and `cheap.test.ts`. The P1-U3 fixture's steps 4 and 6 assert these rows.

## Related

- #6466 (no-runtime message on the hook file; handed over by Scott; D-008, D-013): fixed here. Suggest removing `Upgrade Blocker` and `urgent` after the message fix.
- #5960: the `deft-hook` old-repo path now checks the order and prints the old-layout message; the blocking exit is P1-U1 / P1-U2. Comment when this merges.
- #6375 / #6534 (closed): wording checked here (D-017).
- #6517, #6550: the same message for git hooks and `task` (P4-U3d).
- #6619 (wording), #6201 (P1-U1), #5940 / #6225 (P4-U3b).

## Plan placement

- Unit P4-U3a, story id `ovpr-p4-u3a`. Phase 4, wave 4.2. Size M.
- Depends on P4-U2 (its RC-06 docs PR merged), P1-U1 and P1-U2. O-34 / RC-07 approved, and its docs PR merged, before this merges.
- Blocks P4-U3b, P4-U3c and P4-U3d (they import the table).
- Owner polfer. Scott: FYI only, because `hook-dispatch.ts` sits next to his `decideHook`.
narratives.UserStory: As a developer whose Directive can't run in a checkout, I want every Directive entry point to check in the same order and name the one command that fixes it, so that I am never sent to a command that doesn't work or that the hook then blocks.

Recovery words: drafts/RC-06.md (approved, docs merged as v261118) and drafts/RC-12.md (approved, docs merged as v261118). One PR for all three units (polfer D-037).
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. P4-U3a: packages/core/src/install-health/constants.ts gets `EntrySituation`, `ENTRY_GUARD_MESSAGES`, `projectInstallCommand(projectRoot)` and the order doc comment (disabled -> root-mismatch (hooks) -> legacy-layout (only without a runtime pin) -> runtime-missing -> pin-mismatch/overlay -> contract-too-new (launcher) -> wiring-damaged -> data-behind). Old constant names stay as aliases. Add a row for `FOREIGN_RUNTIME_LINK_RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` (#6563) with unchanged text except where RC-06 rewords it; root-mismatch text moves over unchanged. Align `renderPinMismatchRecoveryGuidance` (#6534, pin-mismatch-guidance.ts) to the pin-mismatch row and O-30 (name only admitted commands). New packages/cli/src/entry-guard.ts = byte-identical launcher copy (node:fs/node:path only) plus a parity test.
2. P4-U3a: adopt in the .mjs outer (host-hook-outer.ts: runtime-missing row with lockfile command, Node built-ins only, no pin check in the outer), global deft-hook (hook-launcher.ts: disabled check, legacy via P1-U2's recogniser and hand-off as already shipped, table rows, renderHookBlock, fix the docstring), and hook-dispatch.ts run() (disable flag first via isDeftDirectiveDisableActive, then decideHook; deny text from the table).
3. P4-U3b: launcher.ts and bookends.ts use `classifyLauncherSituation` (in entry-guard.ts): disabled notice + exit 0 for passthrough commands; one row per situation; no `@?`; doctor prints exactly one Next: line; `RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` in packages/cli/src/constants.ts removed or kept only as the wiring-damaged alias.
4. P4-U3d: Taskfile.yml setup checks `_directive-run.sh` and names `directive install --repair`; GITHOOK_HELPER (setup-wiring.ts) prints the runtime-missing row with a lockfile branch in sh; skill-pointer Recovery line per the AC9.7 table; tasks/engine-invoke.cjs and tasks/engine.yml use the runtime-missing row; packages/runtime/src/bin.ts refuses on pin != installed with the pin-mismatch row (exempt: contract entry points, doctor, --version, --help, hook:dispatch). Regenerate this repo's .githooks/_directive-run.sh (ordinary repair output).
5. Tests per the three specs. Changelog fragment changelog.d/6620-one-hook-guard-and-message-table.md.
narratives.Constraint:
- Recovery words are exactly the approved RC-06 / RC-12 texts (requirements v261118). AC9.7 table (RC-06): runtime missing or not the pinned version -> the project install (`npm install` for npm, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` for pnpm, chosen from the lockfile); wiring damaged while the pinned runtime is installed -> `directive install --repair`; project data behind or an old layout -> `directive upgrade`; `directive` command missing -> `npm i -g @deftai/directive`. AC9.12 (RC-06): on the host-hook path nothing is let through when the runtime is missing, 'so the message says a person runs the install in a terminal'; on pin != installed the pin blocks and lets through only a tool call that is exactly `npm install`, `npm ci` or `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the project root. Old-layout row (RC-12, §A5.6): "This project uses an older version of Directive that isn't installed. Run `npm install` (or `pnpm install`) to keep using it, or run `directive upgrade` to update." Never name plain `pnpm install` for a pin mismatch (O-30), never '(or yarn)', never `npm i -g @deftai/directive, then directive install --repair`, never `deft update`.
- Plain customer wording: no internal acronyms (no 'OVPR', 'pin package', 'AC9.12') in any message a customer sees.
- RC-10 is not approved: leave the launcher `postinstall` in packages/cli/package.json exactly as it is.
- #6594 / #6607 (Scott's root-mismatch admit): change it only as far as the message table requires (moving its text into the table unchanged). Do not change its detection or admit logic. Do not edit packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts (Scott).
- No product logic and no #6313 admit in the .mjs outer (AC9.1); no pin check in the outer. Do not widen the admit list. No install admitted on the missing-runtime path (D-013). Never use another checkout's runtime (AC9.4 / AC9.5); #6517's and #6550's borrow-the-primary design is ruled out.
- The launcher does not import core (AC3.1): use packages/cli/src/entry-guard.ts. Do not run old Directive code except the RC-12 hand-off P1-U2 already shipped. Do not add a runtime dependency to the launcher (#6225 dependency ask is by design).
- Do not change the registered hook command form or sha8 naming, the git-hook helper file name or `run_directive` API, `core.hooksPath` handling, or pre-commit/pre-push gate content.
- OVPR change gate: read ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/OVPR-CHANGE-GATE.md. Do not edit docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/ and do not ship behaviour that departs from the written OVPR requirements or architecture; stop that part and hand back a change proposal.
- Changelog: add the changelog.d fragment named in file_scope; never edit CHANGELOG.md.
narratives.Dependencies: Depends on: P1-U1 and P1-U2 (merged), RC-06 and RC-12 docs (merged, v261118). Blocks: P4-U3c (in G-F, imports the table). Shares packages/cli/src/bookends.ts, packages/cli/src/launcher.ts and packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts with other groups; serialize merges in conflict group hook-entry.

Refs #6375, #6534, #6563, #6594, #6607.

items.title: One message table (`ENTRY_GUARD_MESSAGES`) in core and one byte-identical copy in packages/cli/src/entry-guard.ts; a parity test fails on any drift.

narrative.Acceptance: Given packages/core/src/install-health/constants.ts and packages/cli/src/entry-guard.ts, when packages/cli/src/entry-guard-parity.test.ts runs, then the two tables and the `projectInstallCommand` outputs are equal, and the test fails if either copy changes alone.

items.title: The .mjs outer, global deft-hook and hook-dispatch all check the untracked disable flag before any pin check.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an untracked root `.deft-directive-disable` and a pin mismatch, when the .mjs outer, `deft-hook` or `hook-bin` runs, then each stops quietly (allow / exit 0) without a pin check, and a test covers each entry point.

items.title: In an old-layout project with no project-local old copy installed, deft-hook prints the RC-12 old-layout row and blocks per host; it never runs another copy.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an old-layout fixture (P1-U2 shapes) with no pre-split copy in its own node_modules, when `deft-hook` runs, then it prints "This project uses an older version of Directive that isn't installed. Run `npm install` (or `pnpm install`) to keep using it, or run `directive upgrade` to update." and blocks with the host's blocking response, and no global or out-of-project copy is started.

items.title: With node_modules deleted, the outer and deft-hook print the runtime-missing row with the lockfile-correct command, say a person runs it in a terminal, and block per host.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a project with `pnpm-lock.yaml` (or `package-lock.json`) and no `node_modules`, when the .mjs outer or `deft-hook` runs before a tool call, then it prints the runtime-missing row naming `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (or `npm install`), says a person runs it in a terminal, and blocks per host.

items.title: With pin != installed, hook-bin denies with the pin-mismatch row, and the exact command it names is admitted.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an installed runtime built from this change at a version other than the pin, when `hook-bin` runs for a tool call, then it denies with the pin-mismatch row, and every command that row can name (all three lockfile cases) passes `matchPinMismatchRecoveryCommand`.

items.title: No string in the hook entry points, launcher, launcher doctor, Taskfile, tasks/, git-hook helper or skill pointers contains `npm i -g @deftai/directive, then`, '(or yarn)', `@?` or `deft update` as a fix.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the changed files, when they are searched for `npm i -g @deftai/directive, then`, `(or yarn)`, `@?` and `deft update`, then none of these appears as recovery text.

items.title: The .mjs outer still uses Node built-ins only before loading hook-bin.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the generated outer source, when packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.test.ts runs, then the existing built-ins-only checks pass and the outer has no pin check.

items.title: In the Visage and Evolution old-layout shapes, launcher passthrough commands and `directive doctor` print the old-layout row and exit non-zero (when no project-local old copy is installed); `directive upgrade` behaves as today.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the Visage-shape and Evolution-shape fixtures with no project-local pre-split copy, when a passthrough command or `directive doctor` runs, then it prints the RC-12 old-layout row and exits non-zero, and `directive upgrade` is unchanged.

items.title: With the untracked disable flag, launcher passthrough commands start no runtime and exit 0 with the disabled notice; doctor, install, upgrade, uninstall, --version and --help behave as before.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an untracked root `.deft-directive-disable` and a pin mismatch, when a passthrough command runs, then no runtime starts and it exits 0 with the one-line disabled notice; when `directive doctor`, `install`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`, `--version` or `--help` runs, then behaviour is unchanged.

items.title: Launcher and launcher doctor: runtime missing and pin != installed each print one row naming the lockfile-correct project install; a range or invalid runtime pin prints the 'rectify the pin' row.

narrative.Acceptance: Given runtime-missing, pin-mismatch and range-pin fixtures, when a passthrough command or `directive doctor` runs, then exactly one Next:/Recovery: line is printed: the project install for the first two (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with a pnpm lockfile) and the rectify-the-pin row, with no install command, for the range pin.

items.title: On a fresh install, `task deft:setup` no longer refuses for a missing `_deft-run.sh`; a real miss names `directive install --repair`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a fresh install with `.githooks/_directive-run.sh`, when `task deft:setup` runs, then it passes the hook-file check; given that file missing, then it names `directive install --repair` and not `deft update`.

items.title: With node_modules deleted, `git commit` (pre-commit) fails with the runtime-missing row; with the untracked disable flag it passes silently.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the regenerated git-hook helper and no `node_modules`, when the pre-commit hook runs, then it exits 1 with the runtime-missing row and the lockfile branch; given an untracked `.deft-directive-disable`, then it passes silently.

items.title: With installed != pin, `git commit` and Taskfile verbs fail with the pin-mismatch row (runtime built from this change); `doctor`, `--version` and `--help` still run.

narrative.Acceptance: Given pin 1.2.4 and installed runtime 1.2.3 built from this change, when `node node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/dist/bin.js verify:encoding` runs, then it exits 1 with the pin-mismatch row; when it runs `doctor`, `--version` or `--help`, then the command runs; with equal versions the command runs.

items.title: Every customer-facing message in the table uses plain words: no 'OVPR', no internal AC numbers, no 'pin package'.

narrative.Acceptance: Given `ENTRY_GUARD_MESSAGES`, when its rows are read, then none contains 'OVPR', 'pre-OVPR', an AC number or 'pin package'.

Problem When Directive can't run, an agent host reaches it three ways: the committed `.mjs` hook file, the global `deft-hook` command (old repos), or the runtime's `hook-bin.js`.
Each one checks things in a different order and prints different advice.
The same broken state gets different instructions, and some of them don't work.
In a fresh clone or a new linked worktree, `node_modules` is missing, so the hooks fail closed (AC9.12).
Agent workflows create worktrees all the time, so this is frequent.
The message must say plainly that a person runs the project install in a terminal, because the agent's own shell is blocked (#6466, D-013).

Evidence (origin/master `def527f5e`): - `.mjs` outer (`hostHookOuterSource()`, `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts:259`): untracked disable flag → quiet allow; `hook-bin.js` missing → fail closed; spawn failure → fail closed.
Text `HOST_HOOK_MISSING_PIN_PROJECT_PM_GUIDANCE` (`:22-24`): "Run npm install or pnpm install (or yarn) in this project." Yarn is not supported, and the text doesn't say that a person must run it.
Global `deft-hook` (`packages/cli/src/hook-launcher.ts`, 64 lines): no disable-flag check, no old-layout check.
Every failure prints `RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` (`:27`, `:36`, `:49`) = "npm i -g @deftai/directive, then directive install --repair" (`packages/cli/src/constants.ts:34`).
The docstring at `:4` still says host configs should call `hook-bin.js` directly (superseded by AC9.1 v261027).
Runtime `hook-bin` (`run()`, `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts:386`): root check, then the pin check (`:446`), then self-complete, then `decideHook`.
The disable flag is checked only inside `decideHook` (Scott's `dispatcher.ts`), after the pin checks.
Through global `deft-hook` or an old direct `hook-bin.js` registration, a disabled project with a pin mismatch is blocked instead of stopping quietly.
